citations.desc: Primary conveyances (motor vehicle, rail, air, and marine).
citations.narrative:
During transport from Dulles airport to Fredrick, Maryland on 1 July, 2026 three out of five trucks utilized for the transport
were not maintained within the required temperature range of 45 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit. Documented temperatures
were between 93-96 degrees Fahrenheit at beginning and end of the transport within the three trucks, confirmed by the
driver of truck 4 at the time of USDA inspection on 6 August 2026.
The ambient temperature at the airport pickup location reached 97 degrees according to climate data, and the delivery
location also reached 99 degrees Fahrenheit as part of an anticipated heat wave.
During surface transportation, the ambient temperature inside a primary conveyance used to transport nonhuman
primates must be maintained between 45 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit at all times a nonhuman primate is present.
Correct for all transports after 6 August 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
